real_objective: Advance permanent Brain ownership of all useful Opus 5.5 capabilities by deleting false target obligations while preserving every real model-policy requirement.
material_premises: Current first-party documentation distinguishes client-executed tools from server-executed tools.
For client tools, Claude emits structured actions and the caller executes them and returns results.
For server tools, Anthropic infrastructure executes the tool and returns structured results into the interaction.
Browser and computer use are client toolsets executed by the application.
The model's operative contribution on these surfaces is the policy mapping from observable interaction state and schemas/results to text/thinking/tool actions.
Executor internals not exposed in the model observation trace cannot be a direct causal input to that model policy.

conclusion.primary: The interface-policy normal form is independently supported for the checked documented Opus 5.5 tool surfaces.
conclusion.breakthrough: Intrinsic tool-use capability should be defined modulo trace-equivalent executor substitution: executor implementation variants that preserve the model-visible interface and result trace are the same intrinsic-policy test condition.
conclusion.deletion: Do not create new intrinsic Opus capability obligations merely because a new external tool name or implementation exists.
conclusion.preserve: Continue testing the model-policy functions required to use arbitrary replaceable executors: schema understanding, tool choice, arguments, ordering, observation integration, recovery, coordination, memory/continuity and scope judgment.
conclusion.terminal_truth: This deletes a false infinity but does not supply the missing literal-completeness witness and does not prove terminal completion.

rejected_material_alternatives.reason: Causally misattributes executor computation to the model and creates an artificial open-ended target.
Wrong direction; policy quality over schemas, actions, results, recovery and long horizons remains a real Opus capability target.
The verification does not establish literal target-domain completeness.

uncertainties: Private or undocumented Claude product surfaces may expose additional intrinsic channels.
The current 19-family mapping to the policy basis remains a separate lossless-coverage problem.
Literal all-useful target completeness still lacks W1, W2 or an equivalent sound complete-domain witness.
assumptions: First-party documentation accurately describes the checked public interfaces.
Intrinsic model capability attribution is causal and limited to information/action channels available to the model policy.
non_goals: No redefinition of all useful to currently observed.
No claim Brain already dominates Opus 5.5 policy behavior.
No capability family or ownership promotion.
supersession_conditions: A current first-party surface proves a model-intrinsic execution channel not factorizable as model policy plus external transition.
Canonical target semantics explicitly change to include external executor implementation internals as Opus-owned capability.
A stronger verified ontology theorem strictly subsumes executor-substitution invariance.
